L01.note: 10/11/13/14 tight cluster, nothing distinguishes a member

L02.note: 6 and 20 are the parts, 120 their product, 26 their sum - a sum option with both addends present usually answers a 'total' stem

L03.note: 25 is the hub the others come off (25/2=12.5, 25/5=5), and the hub is the undivided value

L05.note: 190/200/210 evenly spaced with 130 as a far outlier; 200 is the centre of the designed trio

L06.note: 48 is the hub - 42, 32 and 28 are all simple fractions of it, and 48:32 = 42:28

L07.note: 2.04/2.28 are a near-twin pair and 6.36 = 2(2.04)+2.28, so 6.36 is the accumulation distractor

L08.note: 9 is the difference of the two extremes 10 and 1, which are sitting there as the raw inputs

L09.note: 24 sits at the same ratio to 80 as 18 does to 60, making it the computed member of the grid

L11.note: 64 and 100 are round squares and 88 is round; 73 is the only unmanufactured-looking value

L12.note: 2160, 1800, 2700 are all round multiples of 180; 2025 is the odd non-round magnitude

L13.note: 21 and 4 are both options and 5.25 = 21/4, so 5.25 is the value computed from the two intermediates

L14.note: 12, 15, 20 are all round factors of 60; 23 is the odd prime out

L15.note: 260 = 400 - 140, both of which are present as options

L18.note: 45 and 90 are a doubling pair beside 40/100; the undoubled 45 is the likelier base value

L19.note: 4/5 and -4/5 are a sign pair against 5 and -2; the fully sign-and-reciprocal-transformed member is the designed answer

L22.note: 15000/30000/35000 are round; 26250 is the only computed-looking magnitude (= 0.75 x 35000)

L23.note: 9 = 3 squared and 5/-5 is a sign pair, but nothing picks between the two families

L24.note: 480 = 210 + 270 and 60 = 270 - 210, so both combinations are distractors and a base value is the key

L25.note: 10 is the harmonic mean of 30 and 6 (combined-rate shape) with both inputs present as distractors

L26.note: 24 is the harmonic mean of 20 and 30, both present as distractors
